title: Jobs are the test of change
gist: The World Bank Group's FY26 Scorecard frames institutional reform around jobs, reporting $328.7 billion in expected private capital mobilized (up 67% since FY24) and gains on all 15 comparable indicators, while conceding that low-income economies get only about 6% of mobilization and lenders still favor established borrowers.

insights.claim: The World Bank Group says the test of its reform is getting harder because aid budgets are shrinking, debt is squeezing public investment, conflict and climate shocks are eroding livelihoods, and skepticism about international cooperation is rising.
insights.so_what: Multilaterals are under pressure to prove results, pushing them toward private-capital leverage and guarantees.
insights.quote: Aid budgets are shrinking. Debt is squeezing public investment. Conflict and climate shocks are eroding livelihoods.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The World Bank Group's FY26 Scorecard records $328.7 billion in expected private capital mobilized, up 67% since FY24, and $242.5 billion in expected private capital enabled, up 50% since FY25.
insights.so_what: Rapidly growing co-investment pipeline alongside multilaterals in emerging markets.
insights.quote: The Scorecard records $328.7 billion in expected private capital mobilized — up 67 percent since FY24 — and $242.5 billion in expected private capital enabled
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: IFC accounts for about 63% of the World Bank Group's expected private capital mobilization, while IBRD and IDA account for about 71% of expected capital enabled.
insights.so_what: IFC is the main direct co-investment channel; IBRD/IDA work mainly by changing investment conditions.
insights.quote: IFC accounts for about 63 percent of expected mobilization; IBRD and IDA account for about 71 percent of expected capital enabled.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Annual World Bank Group private capital mobilization reached $112 billion in FY26, and the Group issued more than $25 billion in guarantees through a single-access guarantee platform.
insights.so_what: Guarantee capacity at this scale can de-risk EM infrastructure and project finance for private investors.
insights.quote: Annual private capital mobilization reached $112 billion in FY26, and the Group issued more than $25 billion in guarantees
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Low-income economies account for only about 6% of the World Bank Group's expected private capital mobilization.
insights.so_what: Private capital still avoids the poorest markets despite multilateral de-risking, a persistent gap and potential opportunity.
insights.quote: Low-income economies account for only about 6 percent of expected private capital mobilization.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: MIGA helps investors manage political and regulatory risk, extending the World Bank Group's reach into markets where private capital would otherwise not go.
insights.so_what: Political-risk insurance remains a key enabler for investing in frontier markets.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Across the World Bank Group Scorecard portfolio, 326.6 million students received better education, 615 million people accessed quality health services, and 258.4 million people gained electricity access.
insights.so_what: Scale of human-capital and electrification investment underpinning future EM labor supply and demand.
insights.quote: 326.6 million students received better education, 615 million people accessed quality health services, and 258.4 million people gained electricity access.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: All 15 World Bank Group indicators with comparable data show gains since FY24, with access to financial services up 159%, broadband use up 114%, and electricity access up 51%.
insights.so_what: Fast growth in financial and digital access in developing markets supports fintech and telecom demand.
insights.quote: Access to financial services rose 159 percent, broadband use 114 percent, and electricity access 51 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In Uzbekistan, IFC transaction advice and financing plus World Bank payment guarantees enabled the Samarkand and Jizzakh private solar plants, adding 440 MW of capacity and generating more than 930 GWh by project close.
insights.so_what: Shows a replicable template (auctions, contracts, payment guarantees) for private renewable investment in Central Asia.
insights.quote: The Samarkand and Jizzakh plants added 440 megawatts of capacity and generated more than 930 gigawatt-hours by the time the project closed.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Private solar investment in Uzbekistan required credible auctions, workable contracts and confidence that electricity buyers would pay, which payment guarantees helped provide.
insights.so_what: Offtaker credit risk is the binding constraint for EM renewables; guarantees unlock it.
insights.quote: Private solar investment needed credible auctions, workable contracts and confidence that electricity buyers would pay.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In fragile and conflict-affected economies, the World Bank Group Scorecard reports electricity access for 54.8 million people and services and livelihood support for 19.5 million displaced people and host-community members.
insights.so_what: Indicates the scale of multilateral activity in markets most private investors avoid.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: In Morocco's Marrakech-Safi region, IFC advisory support cut public-contract payment times from 39 to 22 days and cleared $14.4 million in arrears.
insights.so_what: Late government payments are a working-capital drag on firms; fixing them is a cheap growth lever.
insights.quote: IFC advisory support helped cut public-contract payment times from 39 to 22 days and clear $14.4 million in arrears.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Ukraine's crop-receipt system, letting farmers use harvests as collateral, is being adapted in the Western Balkans and South Caucasus, and Albania has adopted a Crop and Warehouse Receipts law.
insights.so_what: Spreading warehouse-receipt finance opens new agri-lending markets in the region.
insights.quote: Albania has adopted a Crop and Warehouse Receipts law.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Unpredictable rules, weak credit information or late government payment can prevent a business with workers, customers and a good product from growing.
insights.so_what: Institutional quality, not just demand, determines firm scaling in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Unpredictable rules, weak credit information or a government that pays late can close the path to expansion.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: World Bank support to Ecuador's Corporación Financiera Nacional enabled 22 institutions to provide more than 26,000 sub-loans by end-2025, with an evaluation estimating an 8.9% employment gain among formal firms studied and about 27% among firms without previous bank credit.
insights.so_what: Credit to first-time borrowers yields far higher job returns than lending to established clients.
insights.quote: estimated an 8.9 percent employment gain among the formal firms studied, rising to about 27 percent among firms without previous bank credit.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Ecuador's evaluation found lenders still favored firms with established credit relationships even though employment gains were larger among first-time borrowers, revealing a misallocation of credit.
insights.so_what: Lenders' risk aversion leaves the highest-impact borrowers underserved, an opening for data-driven lenders.
insights.quote: lenders still favored firms with established credit relationships, even though gains were larger among first-time borrowers.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The Horn of Africa DRIVE program, combining drought insurance, savings, payments and livestock markets, reached about 475,000 policyholders and paid out $12.5 million in FY26.
insights.so_what: Index-based climate insurance is scaling in pastoral economies.
insights.quote: reached approximately 475,000 policyholders with $12.5 million in payouts in FY26.
insights.locator: In the Horn of Africa, DRIVE
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The World Bank Group plans a 'More and Better-paid Jobs' indicator that converts gains in labor income into an equivalent number of jobs, with first reporting planned for the IDA21 Mid-Term Review.
insights.so_what: A new jobs metric will shape how multilateral lending is allocated and judged.
insights.quote: It translates gains in labor income — from additional employment and better-paid work — into an equivalent number of jobs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The World Bank Group cautions that not every Scorecard result should be attributed to recent reform, as achievements reflect country leadership and years of partnership.
insights.so_what: Reported gains partly reflect legacy projects, so reform impact may be overstated by headline numbers.
insights.quote: Nor should we attribute every result to recent reform.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
